subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Orion Medical)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@orionmed.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Orion Medical)

Alex — great to meet earlier. Thanks again for walking us through Orion's production requirements. Below is a concise recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- PHI-sensitive workloads require tenancy isolation and strict KMS/HSM controls.
- Recent latency spikes during peak hours (affecting EHR writes and real-time triage flows).
- Unpredictable per-token cost from multi-tenant endpoints; need predictable unit economics for budgeting.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reserved, isolated GPU capacity in a private VPC with KMS-managed keys.
- 99.95% availability SLA for inference endpoints and predictable tail latency targets (p95/p99).
- Autoscaling/burst plan to handle daily auth/triage peaks without cold starts.
- Clear audit logs and SOC2 evidence for security/compliance reviews.

Proposed Redwood Dedicated configuration (initial recommendation):
- Reserved pool: 8 x NVIDIA A100 40GB-equivalent GPUs (can increase based on observed q1 traffic).
- Private deployment: customer VPC peering + dedicated tenancy; KMS/HSM integration for key management.
- Autoscale policy: baseline 50% reserved capacity with scheduled and reactive burst up to 200% during peak windows; pre-warmed nodes for sub-100ms p95 on typical requests.
- Caching & batching: enable KV prefix caching for patient-context tokens, and workload-aware batching to reduce per-token cost.
- SLA: target 99.95% uptime, with escalation path and automatic fallback to regional host if capacity constrained.

High-level cost estimate (placeholder until procurement): monthly committed plan ~USD 55,000/month for the reserved pool above (term options available).

Attachments I’m sending for your procurement and security teams: Orion_MED_RFP_202704.pdf (your RFP included for reference), SOC2_audit_request.xlsx (list of items we'll need to provide).

Next steps / proposed timeline:
1) You: confirm peak concurrency and token throughput numbers (see question below).
2) Redwood: provide an updated commitment quote and draft SOW (3 business days after you confirm throughput).
3) Schedule procurement + security call to review SOC2 evidence and network setup (let's target next Tue/Wed).

Question for sizing: could you confirm typical and peak concurrent inference requests (requests/sec) and average tokens per request during peak windows? That will let us validate the 8 GPU recommendation.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a draft SOW once you confirm the numbers.
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@orionmed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Taylor Chen <taylor.chen@orionmed.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Orion Medical)

Thanks Marissa — very helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Peak concurrency: ~110 requests/sec (we see sustained peaks for 20-30 minute windows during business hours).
- Average tokens per request at peak: ~220 tokens (most requests are short clinical summaries, with some long discharge notes ~1,200 tokens but those are <5% of traffic).
- Multi-region fallback: we will need a secondary region for DR (US-West primary, US-East failover). Can Redwood support cross-region replication for KV cache and fast failover?

We should also confirm the canary plan — we prefer a small canary (5% traffic) for 2 weeks before full cutover.

Taylor (procurement) — I’ve looped you in to start the SOW and procurement timeline.

Alex
Director of Engineering, Orion Medical
alex.barnes@orionmed.com | +1 646 555 4821

Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Orion Medical)

Alex — perfect, that sizing data is exactly what we needed. Quick notes in response:

- Sizing: 110 req/sec @ ~220 tokens/request aligns with our estimate; 8 x A100-equivalent should cover baseline + 2x burst headroom. We’ll rerun a model with the 1,200-token heavy-tail and validate whether an additional small pool should be pre-warmed for large batch jobs.
- Multi-region: yes, Redwood Dedicated supports regional failover. We can replicate KV caches asynchronously (sub-second for most keys) and promote a failover region automatically under the routing policy. We’ll document expected RPO/RTO for DR in the SOW.
- Canary: we recommend the 5% canary for 2 weeks, with stepwise ramp (5% -> 20% -> 60% -> 100%) and automated rollback on quality/latency regressions.

Next steps I’ll take immediately:
- Rishi will draft a term sheet and commitment quote based on the configuration and term length (Rishi, dropping in to confirm: are we ok to start with a 12-month commit with quarterly usage reviews?).
- I’ll schedule a 45-minute procurement/security review for next Tue/Wed; Taylor, what times work for you?
- We'll attach the preliminary SOW and a sample SLA to the HubSpot record once Rishi has the pricing numbers.

—
Marissa
